headline: 5-1 on 6 value plays, +$43.77
paragraphs: 5 games finished in Week 5. It found a playable edge in 4 of them and left the other 1 alone. Those plays went 5-1, worth +$43.77 at $10 a play (73.0% on the $60 at risk).

By market, spreads went 2-0, totals went 1-1 and moneylines went 2-0. The best of them was Pittsburgh ML +160, a 20-point gap between the model and the price that finished Pittsburgh 35, Virginia Tech 33. The one that stung was Under 55 in Pittsburgh at Virginia Tech, a 3.5-point disagreement with the market that finished Pittsburgh 35, Virginia Tech 33.

The five plays that actually got published went 1-0 for +$16.00, ahead of the full board. Ranking by expected value is supposed to concentrate the good ones at the top, and whether it does is something only a season of these will answer.

Season to date the model has made 87 value plays and gone 36-49-2, -$139.44 on flat $10 bets (-16.0%). It expected to win 59% of those and won 42%. On line movement, 1 of the 1 published picks whose numbers moved closed worse than the site posted them, so the market came our way 100% of the time. Sample is getting real enough to argue with, though a model that beats closing lines is rarer than one that beats a few hundred results.
